```{r MARS}
mars_control_function = function(df,
                                 target,
                                 k1,
                                 k2,
                                 num_repeats,
                                 threshold,
                                 n_top_features = c()
){
  cl = makeCluster(6)
  registerDoParallel(cl)
  
  external_perf_df = NULL
  global_perf_df = NULL
  
  external_conf_table_list = list()
  global_conf_table_list = list()
  
  global_coef_df = NULL
  
  threshold_df = df %>% filter(Conc. > threshold) %>% 
    select(-c(Conc., Replicates))
  
  num_feature_array = c(1, n_top_features)
  
  for (rep in 1:num_repeats){
    global_kfold = createFolds(threshold_df[[target]], k = k1)
    
    for (global_fold in 1:k1){
      external_coef_df = NULL
      
      global_train = threshold_df[-global_kfold[[global_fold]], ]
      global_test = threshold_df[global_kfold[[global_fold]], ]
      
      external_resample = rf_resampling_function(
        target = target,
        dataset = global_train,
        n_folds = k2,
        perf_df = external_perf_df,
        coef_df = external_coef_df,
        conf_table_list = external_conf_table_list,
        transformation = c("scale", "center"),
        model_type = "mars"
      )
      
      external_perf_df = external_resample$perf_df
      external_coef_df = external_resample$coef_df
      external_conf_table_list = external_resample$conf_table_list
      
      # Average importance metrics obtained from this global fold
      avg_coefs = data.frame("avg_importance" = colMeans(external_coef_df))
      avg_coefs = avg_coefs %>% arrange(desc(avg_importance))
      avg_coefs$Pairs = row.names(avg_coefs)

      # Subset features by importance metrics
      max_features = length(avg_coefs$avg_importance)
      num_feature_array[1] = max_features
      num_feature_array = num_feature_array[which(num_feature_array <= max_features)]
      
      # Global resample 
      global_resample = multi_feature_global_rf_resampling(
        target = target,
        train = global_train,
        test = global_test,
        sorted_coefs = avg_coefs,
        num_feature_list = num_feature_array,
        perf_df = global_perf_df,
        coef_df = global_coef_df,
        conf_table_list = global_conf_table_list,
        transformation = c("scale", "center"),
        model_type = 'mars'
      )
      
      # Set global data frames to the output of the global resample
      global_conf_table_list = global_resample$conf_table_list
      global_coef_df = global_resample$coef_df
      global_perf_df = global_resample$perf_df
    }
  }
  return(list("external_conf_tables" = external_conf_table_list,
              "external_coef_df" = external_coef_df,
              "external_performance" = external_perf_df,
              "global_conf_tables" = global_conf_table_list,
              "global_coef_df" = global_coef_df,
              "global_performance" = global_perf_df
              # "global_coef_plot" = global_coef_plot
              ))
}

f_test_df = split_dab_df_list[[10]]
mars_test = mars_control_function(df = f_test_df,
                               target = 'target_vector',
                               k1 = 5,
                               k2 = 5,
                               num_repeats = 2,
                               threshold = 0,
                               n_top_features = c(10, 8, 6, 4, 3))

# MARS/EARTH models are entirely compatible with slightly modified rf specific files
# but it may be worth adding the feature importance metric to the y axis, since
# in rfs its impurity, but it's generalized cross validated error with MARS

# Note that I tried to use bagEarth to maybe stabilize the importance metrics
# but I think the code may be bugged, you get an error when trying to use varImp
# with a bagEarth object
coef_viz = rf_coef_visualization(mars_test$global_coef_df)
rf_performance_plotter(mars_test$global_performance)
coef_viz
```



For a given set of input data, the following can increase the speed of the forward pass:
(i) decreasing degree (because there are fewer combinations of terms to consider),
(ii) decreasing nk (because there are fewer forward pass terms),
(iii) increasing minspan (because fewer knots need to be considered),
(iv) decreasing fast.k (because there are fewer potential parents to consider at each
forward step),
(v) increasing thresh (faster if there are fewer forward pass terms).
The backward pass is normally much faster than the forward pass, unless pmethod =
"exhaustive". Reducing nprune reduces exhaustive search time. One strategy is to
first build a large model and then adjust pruning parameters such as nprune using
update.earth.

```{r PLS}
mars_control_function = function(df,
                                 target,
                                 k1,

  threshold_df = df %>% filter(Conc. > threshold) %>% 
    select(-c(Conc., Replicates))
  
  num_feature_array = c(1, n_top_features)

      # Subset features by importance metrics

      num_feature_array[1] = max_features
      num_feature_array = num_feature_array[which(num_feature_array <= max_features)]
      
      # Global resample

      )
      
      # Set global data frames to the output of the global resample

      global_perf_df = global_resample$perf_df
    }
  }
  return(list("external_conf_tables" = external_conf_table_list,
              "external_coef_df" = external_coef_df,
              "external_performance" = external_perf_df,
              "global_conf_tables" = global_conf_table_list,
              "global_coef_df" = global_coef_df,
              "global_performance" = global_perf_df
              # "global_coef_plot" = global_coef_plot
              ))
}
print('fds')
```

```{r}
test_df = f_test_df %>% select(-c(Replicates, Conc.))
trCont = trainControl(method = "repeatedcv",
                      repeats = 3,
                      number = 5)

pls_t = train(target_vector~.,
              data = test_df,
              trControl = trCont,
              method = 'pls')

spls_t = train(target_vector~.,
              data = test_df,
              trControl = trCont,
              method = 'spls')
# Need to get the average and absolute value of these, since it's for each
varImp(pls_t)
varImp(spls_t)
```
